    "reason": "The assertion that a causal attention mask restricts the attention matrix to be lower-triangular relative to the position index is technically incorrect. In a causal (autoregressive) setup where a token at position $t$ attends only to positions $\tau \neq t$ and $\tau < t$, the valid entries are in the lower-left triangle of the matrix (assuming row=source, col=target). The restriction prevents attending to *later* positions ($\tau > t$), which corresponds to zeroing out the *upper*-right triangle. Therefore, the resulting masked matrix is upper-triangular (with zeros below the diagonal if considering valid attention as non-zero above, or more commonly described as an upper-triangular mask applied to logits where $mask_{ij} = 0$ if $j > i$). The claim that it restricts the matrix to be 'lower-triangular' contradicts the definition of preventing attention to later positions. A position cannot attend to later positions implies the future is blocked; in standard matrix notation (row=current, col=next), blocking the future creates an upper-triangular structure of zeros, leaving the lower triangle valid. Thus, stating it restricts the matrix to be 'lower-triangular' is a confusion of terms:",
